title: The schottische and the few pianists who played it
summary: Contest dancing on the schottische and the half-dozen piano players who could play it, including Newman, Udell and Big Bill Thompson.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: The shardest, he played, tell you how he played waltzes.

And that's what I was fixing to say. The waltz and the shardest, that was a popular dance. They contest you on the shardest. Oh, yeah? Yeah. You dance around right and left. You never stop turning. You go all the way to the other hall, and you keep turning. You never give up action. And the same way with the piano. The guy played the piano. He never let up on the beat of the number. The shardest was a hard number all the way for dancing and playing. Very few piano players played the shardest. There was only about six piano players around, I mean, of the time, that played the shardest. And that was fellas like Newman, Udell, Big Bill Thompson, myself.
